findings.explanation: Cassandra reports dropped messages in `system.log` as one summary line per message type every 5 seconds, for example `MUTATION messages were dropped in last 5000 ms: 0 internal and 65 cross node`. The number of log lines measures how many 5-second intervals had any drops, not how many mutations were dropped. A threshold of 10 lines per 5 minutes is therefore not a meaningful rate.
findings.quote: Page when event rate exceeds 10 per 5 minutes outside drills.
findings.suggested_fix: Explain that the alert should extract the internal and cross-node counts from the `<TYPE> messages were dropped in last 5000 ms` lines (with `TYPE` set to MUTATION, READ, and so on) and threshold on their sum per host per 5 minutes. Alternatively, use the JMX `DroppedMessage` metrics.

findings.explanation: No Splunkbase add-on defines these sourcetypes, so they are custom. The text never names the log file paths (`/var/log/cassandra/system.log`, `gc.log`), the log lines that matter (MessagingService dropped-message summaries, ReadTimeoutException or WriteTimeoutException stack traces, GCInspector pause lines), or the fact that `pause_time_ms` must be extracted by the customer.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the files and the exact message patterns, and state that `cassandra:system` and `cassandra:gc` are custom sourcetypes needing props.conf line-breaking (multi-line Java stack traces) and a `pause_time_ms` extraction.

findings.explanation: `TRANSFORMS-` classes in props.conf run at index time. Search-time field extraction for these values is normally done with `EXTRACT-` or `REPORT-`, which do not need a re-index when the pattern changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `EXTRACT-` (inline regex) or `REPORT-` (transforms.conf) in props.conf for `keyspace`, `table` and `coordinator`.

findings.explanation: Collection is a Universal Forwarder file monitor, so poll intervals, HEC tokens, 'vendor API' HTTP 401/429 errors and 'vendor admin UI inventory count' do not apply. The text gives no `[monitor://]` stanza and no comparison with `nodetool tpstats` dropped counts.
findings.quote: Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cassandra:system, cassandra:gc into database. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds
findings.suggested_fix: Give `[monitor:///var/log/cassandra/system.log]` and `gc.log` stanzas with the sourcetypes and `index=database`. For validation, compare the summed dropped counts in Splunk with the 'Dropped' section of `nodetool tpstats` on the same node.

findings.explanation: The explanation repeats the title and says nothing concrete. It does not explain that the database is throwing away writes or failing to answer reads in time because a node is overloaded or paused.
findings.quote: We watch Cassandra Dropped Mutations and Read Timeouts so we can keep this part of the data platform within the capacity and quality targets our teams expect.
findings.suggested_fix: Explain that when a database node is overloaded or frozen for a moment, it can give up on saving some changes or answering some requests in time. We warn you when that starts happening often on a server.

findings.explanation: The SPL outputs only `events` and `kinds` per host and 5-minute bucket. It never computes a maximum GC pause, so this overlay needs a separate search.
findings.suggested_fix: Either note that the GC overlay comes from a separate `max(pause_time_ms)` timechart, or drop it.

findings.explanation: The 'Timeouts' title points at the documentation root. The HEC and savedsearches.conf references are generic and unrelated to file-monitored Cassandra logs.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the Cassandra metrics page (DroppedMessage metrics) and the `cassandra.yaml` request-timeout settings, and replace HEC with the Splunk monitor-input documentation.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The search term "DroppedMutation" does not appear in Cassandra `system.log`, which writes `MUTATION messages were dropped in last 5000 ms: ...`. The dropped-mutation half of the detection matches nothing. "Operation timed out" is mainly a client or driver message.

GC-pause events are counted together with timeout lines toward `events >= 10`, mixing cause and symptom. The `rex "(Read|Write|CAS) timeout"` pattern will not match exception class names such as `ReadTimeoutException`.
Counting log lines measures 5-second report intervals, not dropped messages. Extract and sum the internal and cross-node counts.

summary: The goal is sound, but the search keys on a token (`DroppedMutation`) that Cassandra's `system.log` does not write. The 'more than 10 events per 5 minutes' rule counts 5-second summary lines rather than dropped messages. Implementation, data-source, plain-language and reference text are generic or describe collection steps that do not apply to a file-monitored log.
